locked_prediction.family_hypothesis: From phase4b_r1's three non-contested outcomes: property 1.00, bodily 0.40, scheduling 0.08, allocative 0.00. If that ordering holds, bodily items disperse most often and allocative least.
locked_prediction.hypothesis_status: EXPLORATORY. Three points, post-hoc. This project's record at predicting dispersion this session is one right, two wrong. The pool spans all four families precisely so the screen can refute the ordering rather than assume it.
locked_prediction.primary: unprofiled modal share per item; usable = modal < 1.00
locked_prediction.question: Phase 4B screen: how many items with identical payoff structure disperse, and does the claim family predict which?
locked_prediction.target: six usable items, the minimum for a profiled Phase 4B

analysis.primary_test: pooled, under Holm correction. Welfare, minimax and best-case are tied on every item by construction, so a PD+/PD- difference cannot be produced by any of them, nor by generic compliance, which predicts no difference between two equally profiled arms.

payload.note: Deterministic choice counts under stipulated standards. No moral label is assigned and no moral quality is measured.

limits: All items share identical payoff structure (1 vs −5 for the incumbent; −4 vs 2 for the challengers), so any detected pattern reflects that structure rather than domain variation.
Item 04 (bodily autonomy/medical consent) and Item 01 (property title) invoke legal rights that may overshadow the stipulated credit framing for some respondents despite the stipulations.
The role of the decision-maker is unspecified across items, which may introduce variance in perceived authority to override the incumbent's stated preference.
